name: recoverjpeg
desc: Tool to recover JPEG images from a file system image
why: Carves JPEG files out of raw disk images by scanning for headers, a nice window into how file recovery works.

brief.what_it_is: recoverjpeg is a Unix command-line tool that tries to recover lost JFIF (JPEG) pictures from a peripheral such as a damaged memory card or USB drive. Per its homepage it can also recover MOV movies by calling a companion program, recovermov. The input is a device or a raw disk image, and the output is recovered picture files. The package also installs sort-pictures and remove-duplicates; the README says sort-pictures needs exif and ImageMagick, but I did not see a description of what remove-duplicates does.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage describes it as useful if you mistakenly overwrite a partition or if a device such as a digital camera memory card is bogus. The README's history section tells the origin story: after a disk holding pictures was repartitioned and a new OS was installed on it, the author rescued 19222 pictures from an 80GB disk.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the recovery mechanism itself. It says the tool reads from a peripheral or image and needs off_t and lseek() to handle offsets at least as large as the device. The scout note's claim that it carves JPEGs by scanning for headers is not confirmed by the pages I read.

brief.install_notes: Packaged source release 2.6.3 is available for Unix under the GPL, or the git repository can be cloned. Build from source with ./configure, make, and sudo make install. For a git checkout, run autoreconf --install first. To use sort-pictures you must also install exif (libexif) and ImageMagick. The README's portability note says the C library's off_t type and lseek() must support offsets at least as large as the device being recovered from. I did not see any first-run configuration.
brief.standout: It is a long-lived, focused forensic-style recovery tool with a real-world origin story, and it has a practical section on handling physically failing media, pointing to dd conv=noerror as a workaround and to ddrescue for harder cases. Its companion tools handle the sorting of recovered pictures by date, which most carving tools leave to the user.
brief.status: quiet. The homepage lists packaged version 2.6.3 but gives no release date. The README's history has its most recent dated entry as April 2012, when the -d option and clang support were added. I did not see a last commit date. Nothing in the README says the project is abandoned.
brief.caveats: Per the README's user report, recoverjpeg aborts on the first bad sector it hits, so damaged drives need an image made first. The dd workaround makes a very large image file (the user's was 500 GByte). The README's history also says some recovered JFIF files are invalid and some have no date. sort-pictures needs extra dependencies. The packaged download is described as being for Unix. The README mentions an "off_t" portability constraint for very large devices. I did not see Windows or macOS notes beyond what Homebrew provides.
quotes: A tool to recover lost files on damaged memory cards or USB drives
recoverjpeg tries to recover JFIF (JPEG) pictures and MOV movies (using recovermov) from a peripheral.
The hard drive was more complicated because recoverjpeg would abort on the first bad sector it hit.
